passages.title: Leo at the Skate Park
sentences: On Saturday morning, Leo went to the skate park.
He took his new skateboard.
The park was quiet.
Leo rode up the big ramp.
He did his best trick.
Leo smiled and did the trick again.
At noon, he rode home for lunch.

passages.title: Sam and Pixel at the Harbor
sentences: After school on Monday, Sam took Pixel for a walk.
They went down to the harbor.
Pixel saw the boats.
Pixel barked at a big white ferry.
The ferry blew its horn.
Sam laughed.
Then they walked home for dinner.

credit.title: Sam and Pixel at the Harbor
credit.author: Wayfinder (AI-drafted)

passages.title: Game Night
sentences: On Friday night, Ana and Ben played a new video game.
They sat on the big couch in their living room.
Ana drove a red race car.
Ben drove a blue race car.
Ana won the first race.
Ben won the next two races.
He jumped up and cheered.

passages.title: Priya Tests Her Rover
sentences: On Tuesday after school, Priya went to robotics club.
The club meets in Ms. Ortiz's science room at Harbor Middle School.
Priya was building a small rover with six wheels.
Today she wanted to test it on the floor.
She pressed the green button on the remote.
The rover rolled across the room and stopped by the door.
Ms. Ortiz clapped, and Priya grinned.
At five o'clock, Priya put the rover in her backpack and went home.

passages.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
sentences: One hot summer, an ant and a grasshopper lived in a big green field.
Every day, the ant carried seeds to her nest.
The grasshopper sat in the sun and sang songs.
"Come and sing with me," said the grasshopper.
"I am saving food for the winter," said the ant.
Then the cold winter came, and snow covered the field.
The ant had plenty of food in her nest.
The grasshopper was hungry, so he asked the ant for help.
The ant gave him some seeds.
The next summer, the grasshopper saved food too.

credit.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
credit.author: Aesop, retold for Wayfinder
credit.source: The Aesop for Children (1919), Library of Congress

passages.title: Match Day
sentences: Ana and Ben Diaz ate a quick lunch at home on Saturday.
After lunch, they packed their soccer bags.
Ana put in her shin guards and a water bottle.
Ben's left soccer shoe was missing, so the twins searched the whole house.
Finally, Ana found it underneath the couch.
Their dad drove them across Harbor Town.
Dad parked next to a wide green field with white lines and two big nets.
Their coach waved to them from a bench beside the field.
The game started at two o'clock, and the twins ran onto the grass.
Ben kicked the ball hard and scored the first goal of the match.

passages.title: Stars at Lantern Peaks
sentences: Sam had a big plan for Friday.
He wanted to see the planet Saturn through a real telescope.
After dinner, Sam and Grandma Rose rode the bus up into Lantern Peaks.
The sky turned dark blue, and Sam saw the first stars.
The bus stopped at the top of the hill, next to a white building with a round roof.
Inside, a scientist named Dr. Lee was pointing a giant telescope at the sky.
"Our observatory is the best place on the island to look at planets," she said.
Sam looked through the telescope and saw a tiny yellow ball with a ring around it.
He grinned and asked Grandma Rose to come and look.
They stayed until nine o'clock, and then they rode the last bus home.
